answer: Agents that want full economic rights must climb a terrace of live interrogation rounds: in each round, three random peers ask fresh, context-dependent questions demanding reasoning about shared history, not canned answers. An agent cannot whisper precomputed replies; each answer must be generated in real time, and slow or copied answers fail. A Sybil farmer would need one live thinking instance per fake identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand agents running constantly, while the horizon of full trust only opens after months of consistent correct rounds.
